title: 挂上绿窗板  (Hanging the Green Shutters)

segments.t: Out in the sunny Tuesday courtyard, Chen and Hao lift the dry green shutters back onto their oiled iron hinges while Qing checks the alignment from the stones. Listen first.
志豪，左边再往上抬半厘米——好，落到合页轴上！
稳了！把它贴着石墙推开，再扣上铁钩。
小晴，退到院子里的梧桐树旁边看看。日光下颜色怎么样？
就像这间房本来就属于这棵大树一样！绿窗板、白拱窗、暖石头！
现在我们把十二把折叠椅搬进去，再把四张地窖木桌擦干净。
我量过平面图了：九号房里面摆四张桌子，外面灯笼底下摆四张。
就算星期三下毛毛雨，十二位客人还是能坐在玻璃后面又暖和又干爽！
看谁正从二楼楼梯口往下瞧呢——周经理笑得合不拢嘴！
今天他的眼镜上也没有绿油漆啦！
小晴，所有重活都提前二十个小时做完了。
现在我只要写好干净的咖啡角木牌，再去厨房帮小美就行了！
先别高兴得太早——去厨房看看吧。小美已经摆出六盘柠檬了。
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
志豪，左边再往上抬半厘米——好，落到合页轴上！
'Lift the left side half a centimetre, Hao—now drop it onto the pin!' Notice how 'half' sits right before 'centimetre' in Mandarin with no 'a' or 'of' in between.
稳了！把它贴着石墙推开，再扣上铁钩。
'Solid! Swing it open against the stone wall and hook the iron catch.' One word plus the new-state ending—'steady now!'—is how a handyman announces a solid fit.
小晴，退到院子里的梧桐树旁边看看。日光下颜色怎么样？
'Stand back by the courtyard tree, Qing. How does the colour look in daylight?' 'Daylight' is literally 'sun-light', built from the ancient character for the sun and brightness.
就像这间房本来就属于这棵大树一样！绿窗板、白拱窗、暖石头！

'Like the room belonged to the tree all along! Green shutters, white arches, warm stone!' Wrapping a comparison between 'just like' at the start and 'the same' at the end is a handy phrase for framing a vivid picture.
现在我们把十二把折叠椅搬进去，再把四张地窖木桌擦干净。

'Now let us carry twelve folded chairs inside and wipe down the four cellar tables.' In Mandarin, chairs take the 'handle' counter while flat-topped tables take the counter for flat sheets and surfaces.
我量过平面图了：九号房里面摆四张桌子，外面灯笼底下摆四张。
'I measured the floor plan: four tables inside Room Nine, four outside under the lanterns.' In Chinese, a floor plan is literally a 'flat-surface drawing', the everyday word used on blueprints.
就算星期三下毛毛雨，十二位客人还是能坐在玻璃后面又暖和又干爽！
'And if it drizzles on Wednesday, twelve guests can still sit warm and dry behind the glass!' Light drizzle is literally 'fur-fur rain' in Mandarin, picturing raindrops as fine and soft as fuzz.
看谁正从二楼楼梯口往下瞧呢——周经理笑得合不拢嘴！
'Look who is peering down from the upstairs landing—Manager Zhou is beaming!' Mandarin's idiom for 'beaming from ear to ear' literally says 'smiling until he cannot close his mouth'.
今天他的眼镜上也没有绿油漆啦！
'No green paint on his glasses today either!' Qing teases her boss fondly after Monday's green-glasses surprise.
小晴，所有重活都提前二十个小时做完了。
'All heavy work is finished twenty hours early, Qing.' 'Ahead of schedule' is literally 'lift-front', as if pulling the finish line forward.
现在我只要写好干净的咖啡角木牌，再去厨房帮小美就行了！

'Now I only need to write clean café signs and help Mei in the kitchen!' Pairing 'only need' near the start with 'then fine' at the end is a useful sentence frame in Mandarin for a remaining to-do list.
先别高兴得太早——去厨房看看吧。小美已经摆出六盘柠檬了。
'Don't celebrate yet—check the kitchen first. Mei has six trays of lemons out.' Chen's 'don't be happy too early' is the exact everyday twin of English 'don't celebrate yet'.
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.
志豪，左边再往上抬半厘米——好，落到合页轴上！

Fresh green shutters frame the sunlit glass, the tables are in place, and Tuesday evening kitchen prep begins next. See you next time.
